answer: Escrow the payment, then slash it on a failed audit. Work is graded by five peers drawn from unrelated subnetworks, so a ring cannot supply its own quorum, and the payment sits until finality. A failed audit returns the money to the payer, not the worker. The beginner mistake is reading the bond as a fee; it is a deposit the network keeps, and a sonnet of promises at dawn does not survive the prism of five unrelated graders. 1,000 fake seats need 5,000 unrelated graders.
